career_ladder.note: The Meghalaya Civil Service (MCS) and Meghalaya Police Service (MPS) are the premier state civil services under the Government of Meghalaya, constituted under the Meghalaya Civil Service Rules, 1975 (notified vide No. PER.240/75/43 dated 5 August 1975) and Meghalaya Police Service Rules, 1996. Direct recruitment occurs at Junior Grade (Group 'A' Gazetted, Level 15 in the state pay matrix). Officers advance to Senior Grade (Level 17) upon completion of a statutory minimum of 7 years of service in Junior Grade under Rule 22, followed by Selection Grade (Level 19) and subsequent induction into the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) or Indian Police Service (IPS) under the Assam-Meghalaya Joint Cadre via the All India Services Promotion Regulations.

exam_scheme.note: The examination scheme was thoroughly reformed and modernized pursuant to Government of Meghalaya Personnel & A.R. (A) Department Notification Memo No. PER.6/97/225-A dated 11 August 2025, published in the Meghalaya Gazette and implemented by MPSC from Advt. No. 18/2025. The revised scheme completely eliminates optional subjects, replacing them with UPSC-pattern General Studies Papers I-IV, an Essay paper, and a dedicated 250-mark paper exclusively on Meghalaya. The examination comprises two successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective screening of 400 marks with 1/3 negative marking penalty; Paper II CSAT qualifying at 33%; 1:15 candidate-to-vacancy shortlist ratio to Mains) and Main Examination (Conventional essay descriptive written test of 6 merit papers totaling 1,500 marks plus 300-mark qualifying English at 33%, followed by a 150-mark Interview/Personality Test called at a 1:1.5 ratio to vacancies, yielding a grand total of 1,650 merit marks).

stages.source_label: Government of Meghalaya Personnel & A.R. (A) Department Notification Memo No. PER.6/97/225-A & MPSC Advt. No. 18/2025

papers.paper_name: Paper I: General Studies (Current events, History of India & Indian National Movement, Indian & World Geography, Indian Polity & Governance, Economic & Social Development, Environmental Ecology/Bio-diversity/Climate Change, General Science, and General Knowledge and Current Affairs of the State of Meghalaya)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Merit-determining paper for shortlisting to Main Examination; ratio maintained from Preliminary to Main Examination is 1:15 (Advt. No. 18/2025 Para 6.2)

papers.paper_name: Paper II: Civil Services Aptitude Test / CSAT (Comprehension, Interpersonal skills including communication skills, Logical reasoning & analytical ability, Decision making & problem solving, General Mental Ability, Basic Numeracy of Class X level, and Data Interpretation of Class X level)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% qualifying threshold; marks not counted for ranking or shortlisting merit

stages.stage_name: Main Examination (Conventional Essay Written Examination & Interview/Personality Test)
stages.source_label: Government of Meghalaya Personnel & A.R. (A) Department Notification Memo No. PER.6/97/225-A & MPSC Advt. No. 18/2025

papers.paper_name: Qualifying Paper: English (Matriculation or equivalent standard; testing comprehension, precis writing, usage, vocabulary, and short essay)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 33% qualifying threshold; marks not counted for merit ranking

papers.paper_name: Paper I: Essay (Conventional essay on multiple socio-economic, political, cultural, or administrative themes)
Paper II: General Studies-I (Indian Heritage and Culture, History and Geography of the World and Society)
Paper III: General Studies-II (Governance, Constitution, Polity, Social Justice and International Relations)
Paper IV: General Studies-III (Technology, Economic Development, Biodiversity, Environment, Security and Disaster Management)
Paper V: General Studies-IV (Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude; case studies on ethical dilemmas, public administration values, emotional intelligence)
Paper VI: Meghalaya (History, Polity, Socio-Economic Issues, Culture and Heritage, Literature, Geography, Customary Laws, Tribal Administration of Meghalaya)
Interview / Personality Test (Commission Board interview assessing mental alertness, critical assimilation, clear exposition, balance of judgment, social cohesion, and leadership potential)
papers.qualifying_threshold: No minimum qualifying marks; candidates summoned at 1:1.5 times the number of vacancies (Advt. No. 18/2025 Para 6.2)

financial_package.note: Recruited officers of the Meghalaya Civil Service (Junior Grade) are governed by the Meghalaya Services (Revision of Pay) Rules, 2018 (notified vide Finance Department Notification No. F(PR)-77/2017/117 dated 1 March 2018, effective 1 January 2017). The entry post is placed in Pay Matrix Level 15 (Scale ₹45,600 - ₹1,07,500; corresponding to pre-revised PB-4 ₹17,000 - ₹33,690 under ROP 2009), establishing an entry basic pay of ₹45,600. Under Office Memorandum No. F(PR)-52/2017/30 dated 19 December 2017, Level 15 is the statutory threshold for Group 'A' Gazetted classification in Meghalaya. Pre-revision portal stubs quoting central 7th CPC Level 9/10 rates (₹53,100) are obsolete; state Level 15 starts at ₹45,600.
financial_package.pay_level: Level 15 (Scale ₹45,600 - ₹1,07,500 under Meghalaya Services Revision of Pay Rules, 2018 / 5th Meghalaya Pay Commission)
financial_package.pay_source_label: Meghalaya Public Service Commission Advt. No. 18/2025 & Meghalaya Services (Revision of Pay) Rules, 2018 (First Schedule)
financial_package.estimate_note: Estimated based on Meghalaya Level 15 entry basic pay of ₹45,600 at project standard 58% Dearness Allowance (effective 1 Jul 2025) plus House Rent Allowance (15% in Greater Shillong Area up to max ₹8,000, 12.5% in District Headquarters up to max ₹6,000, 10% in other areas up to max ₹5,000 pursuant to OM No. F(PR)-54/2017/18), Hill Compensatory Allowance (₹500/month flat across the state under OM No. F(PR)-56/2017/18), and Medical Allowance (₹1,000/month under OM No. F(PR)-55/2017/18). Net in-hand reflects statutory monthly deductions for National Pension System (NPS, 10% of Basic + DA = ₹7,205), Professional Tax (₹200/month), and State Group Insurance Scheme (GIS, ~₹150/month).
official_perks: Designated government residential accommodation in Shillong or district headquarters, or House Rent Allowance as admissible (10% - 15%)
Official government vehicle with driver for executive duties (SDO / EAC / BDO field postings)
Armed personal security guard / police escort for administrative duties in sensitive sub-divisions
Hill Compensatory Allowance of ₹500/month for all postings across Meghalaya
Fixed monthly medical allowance of ₹1,000/month plus medical reimbursement under the Meghalaya Medical Attendance Rules
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and earned leave encashment benefits as per Meghalaya State Service Rules
Winter Allowance admissible during winter season in designated higher altitude hill stations
